signals.brief_en:
Title: mohamedsorour1998/Grace

Brief: Grace is an AI‑driven assistance agent designed to reduce benefit loss for families due to paperwork lapses. It continuously monitors Medicaid and SNAP renewal deadlines, automatically files straightforward renewals, and flags ambiguous or high‑impact decisions for human review. The system is built on Strands Agents integrated with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, leveraging large‑language models for document parsing and deadline tracking while maintaining a human‑in‑the‑loop for final adjudication. Current operational data are limited; effectiveness will depend on integration with state portals and the accuracy of source data.

signals.title: Towards Scalable and Cost-Efficient Vulnerability Detection: A Study on Automatic Query Generation
signals.content: Static analysis remains a cornerstone of software security, yet the effectiveness of tools such as CodeQL is often limited by the substantial manual effort required to develop high-coverage query suites. While large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a potential solution for automated code reasoning, their practical utility in generating structured, executable security queries remains underexplored. In this paper, we conduct an empirical study to evaluate the ability of LLMs to synthesize CodeQL queries using vulnerability data from the National Vulnerability Database. Through this investigation, we explore the potential of using LLMs as an automatic CodeQL query generator. Subsequently, we systematically evaluate the performance of various LLM architectures across a diverse set of real-world vulnerabilities, measuring their ability to improve detection coverage and precision. Our findings reveal that LLM-generated queries significantly enhance the baseline CodeQL queries, yielding 82% improvement in average F1-score. Furthermore, we provide a detailed cost- benefit analysis showing that while direct LLM-based scanning of entire repositories is often computationally and financially prohibitive, leveraging LLMs to synthesize CodeQL queries offers a scalable and cost-effective alternative for large-scale vulnerability detection. Our results suggest that LLMs can effectively bridge the gap between unstructured vulnerability reports and formal static analysis specifications, offering a scalable path toward comprehensive automated vulnerability detection.

signals.brief_en:
Title: Towards Scalable and Cost‑Efficient Vulnerability Detection – Automatic Query Generation

Static analysis is essential for software security, but tools like CodeQL depend on manually crafted query suites, limiting coverage. Large language models (LLMs) can reason about code, yet their capacity to produce structured, executable security queries is not well documented. This study empirically assesses LLMs’ ability to generate CodeQL queries from National Vulnerability Database (NVD) entries. Multiple LLM architectures were tested on a broad set of real‑world vulnerabilities, measuring detection coverage and precision. Results show LLM‑generated queries raise the baseline CodeQL F1‑score by 82 % on average. A cost‑benefit analysis indicates that direct LLM scanning of whole repositories is often computationally and financially infeasible, whereas using LLMs to synthesize CodeQL queries provides a scalable, cost‑effective approach for large‑scale vulnerability detection. The findings suggest LLMs can reliably translate unstructured vulnerability reports into formal static‑analysis specifications, enhancing detection without prohibitive resource demands.

signals.title: Emergency Department Revisit Quality Review Screening: Exploring Human Decision-Making and Artificial Intelligence Support
signals.content: Background: Emergency Department (ED) return visits are commonly reviewed for quality assurance, but are often limited (e.g., to revisits within 48-72 hours) to increase actionable finding yield while minimizing chart review burden. Those limitations may lead to missed quality improvement opportunities. Methods: We conducted an exploratory, retrospective study of randomly selected ED visits to a multihospital health system having an ED revisit within 1-14 days to the same health system. Given only each visit's primary diagnosis, raters (2-3 clinicians and GPT-4 large language model [LLM]) assessed characteristics of the diagnosis pairs, including the "target": whether a pair warranted further assessment. Informed by rater response analyses, an algorithm leveraging an LLM-populated knowledge graph ("KGA") was created to automatically screen for potentially concerning pairs, then preliminarily assessed. Results: 99 diagnosis pairs were included. GPT-4 responses poorly correlated to clinician raters, rating nearly all (94%) pairs as warranting follow-up (4.4-13.3 times more than clinicians). However, prompt engineering was minimal. Among clinician raters, revisit medical gravity was consistently significantly associated with the target, while a differential diagnosis/complication composite was significantly associated on unadjusted, but not adjusted (though less powered) analysis. The KGA achieved 83-100% positive predictive value for at least one clinician rater determining further assessment was warranted based on the diagnosis pair. Conclusion: These results can inform next steps for improving screening with LLMs like ChatGPT. Further research is warranted to validate this preliminary work's finding that the KGA may enable enhancing the scope and yield of screening without substantially increasing reviewer workload.

signals.brief_en:
Emergency Department Revisit Quality Review Screening: Exploring Human Decision-Making and Artificial Intelligence Support
Background: Quality reviews of ED return visits usually focus on short windows (48‑72 h) to limit workload, potentially missing improvement opportunities. Methods: A retrospective sample of ED visits with a return within 1‑14 days was examined. Using only the primary diagnosis of each visit, 2‑3 clinicians and GPT‑4 rated whether the diagnosis pair warranted further assessment. Results informed a knowledge‑graph algorithm (KGA) that screens for concerning pairs. Findings: Of 99 diagnosis pairs, GPT‑4 flagged 94 % as needing follow‑up, far exceeding clinicians (who flagged far fewer). Clinician ratings showed that higher medical gravity of the revisit was consistently linked to the need for further assessment; a composite of differential diagnosis/complication was associated in unadjusted analysis only. The KGA achieved 83‑100 % positive predictive value for at least one clinician deeming a pair worthy of review. Conclusion: Simple AI prompts over‑estimate follow‑up needs, but a structured LLM‑driven knowledge graph can reliably prioritize ED revisit pairs for quality review, supporting more efficient human oversight.

signals.title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference-Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs
signals.content: Video understanding has rapidly evolved toward video large language models (VideoLLMs): systems that couple video representations with pretrained large language models and condition generation on a textual prompt. Their strong performance on captioning, question answering, retrieval and temporal grounding comes at a computation and memory cost that grows with frame count and context length, limiting deployment in real-time, mobile and resource-constrained settings. This survey covers inference-efficiency mechanisms for visual and audiovisual VideoLLMs that report concrete reductions in parameter count, FLOPs per input, latency, memory, or visual and audio token count. We analyze bottlenecks across frame sampling, modality encoding, connector-level token reduction, and LLM prefilling and decoding. We organize methods by the pipeline stage at which they act, covering VideoLLMs developed since late 2022 together with earlier frame-sampling and vision-encoder mechanisms that remain components of current pipelines. We assemble literature-reported accuracy--cost comparisons under shared host models and input protocols wherever available, distinguish them from heterogeneous cross-paper evidence, and identify gaps in audiovisual efficiency and standardized evaluation. We maintain a repository at https://github.com/momentslab/awesome-efficient-videollm.

signals.brief_en:
Title: Why Is Video Still So Expensive? A Survey of Inference‑Efficiency Mechanisms in Video and Audiovisual LLMs

VideoLLMs combine video encoders with large language models to enable captioning, QA, retrieval, and temporal grounding. Their performance scales with frame count and context length, creating high FLOP, memory, and latency demands that hinder real‑time, mobile, and low‑resource deployment. This survey catalogs concrete efficiency techniques that reduce parameters, FLOPs, latency, memory, or token counts. It examines bottlenecks in frame sampling, modality encoding, connector‑level token reduction, and LLM prefilling/decoding. Methods are organized by pipeline stage and cover VideoLLMs released since late‑2022, as well as earlier encoder and sampling approaches still used today. Reported accuracy‑cost trade‑offs are compiled where comparable host models and inputs exist; heterogeneous results are flagged. The review highlights gaps in audiovisual efficiency research and the lack of standardized benchmarks. A curated repository is maintained at https://github.com/momentslab/awesome-efficient-videollm.

العنوان: لماذا لا يزال الفيديو مكلفًا؟ مسح لآليات كفاءة الاستدلال في نماذج اللغة الكبيرة للفيديو والوسائط المتعددة

نماذج اللغة الكبيرة للفيديو (VideoLLMs) تدمج مشفرات الفيديو مع نماذج اللغة الكبيرة لتوليد شروحات، إجابات أسئلة، استرجاع، وتحديد زمني. أداءها يزداد مع عدد الإطارات وطول السياق، ما يؤدي إلى استهلاك عالٍ للعمليات (FLOPs) والذاكرة وزمن الاستجابة، مما يحد من استخدامها في الوقت الحقيقي أو على الأجهزة المحمولة أو في بيئات ذات موارد محدودة. يقدم هذا المسح تقنيات كفاءة ملموسة تقلل عدد المعاملات، FLOPs لكل مدخل، زمن الاستجابة، الذاكرة أو عدد الرموز البصرية والسمعية. يحلل الاختناقات في اختيار الإطارات، ترميز الوسائط، تقليل الرموز على مستوى الموصل، ومرحلة التمهيد/التوليد في نموذج اللغة. تُرتب الأساليب حسب مرحلة خط الأنابيب وتغطي نماذج VideoLLM منذ أواخر 2022، بالإضافة إلى أساليب الترميز واختيار الإطارات السابقة التي لا تزال تُستَخدم. تُجمع مقارنات الدقة‑التكلفة المبلغ عنها عندما تكون النماذج والبروتوكولات موحدة؛ وتُميز النتائج المتباينة بين الأوراق. يسلط الاستعراض الضوء على الفجوات في كفاءة الوسائط المتعددة ونقص المعايير الموحدة للتقييم. يُحافظ على مستودع منظم على https://github.com/momentslab/awesome-efficient-videollm.

signals.brief_ar: أفاد باحث أمان أن تطبيقًا حكوميًا سعوديًا، تم تثبيته على أكثر من 10 ملايين جهاز، تضمن بطريق الخطأ مفتاحًا خاصًا وبيانات اعتماد API تابعة للبنك الوطني السعودي. تم إزالة المكوّنات المتأثرة من التطبيق، وتزعم الجهة المورِّدة أن البيانات تم تدويرها، إلا أن التحقق المستقل من عملية التدوير غير متوفر. لم يتم نسخ أي قيم سرية.
